purpose: Test admission-only remaining-lifetime pressure without changing accepted-frame deadlines, storage or repair limits.
method: Production/candidate/production, daemons retained through each ascending four-rate sweep. Same Linux 6.8 container harness and disjoint CPU placement as preceding UDP controls. No local build, kernel test or Git packing overlaps load. Separate Linux 7.0 correctness checks run on another machine. CPU uses before/sent process and thread tick differences; 100% is one core. Delivered rates use receiver sample byte/time deltas. Missing uses final receive counts after drain. Worker/counter deltas include drain.
candidate: For a lane with unsent original bytes, inspect its first unfinished original in the current non-repair batch and its pending-original queue head. Reject only a new arriving source if the earlier deadline is at or before now plus half the current RTT-derived retention lifetime. Keep the existing 2 MiB cap. Existing accepted sources, tails, repairs, deadlines and packet accounting are unchanged. This is a remaining-lifetime heuristic, not exact oldest age. Unexpanded-only backlog with no materialized head retains only the byte check.
counter_units: tx_fresh_guard_checks, tx_fresh_guard_no_head and tx_fresh_guard_drops count sources after existing physical-capacity checks. Guard drops are included in tx_backlog_drops and queue_drops. GSO sources can contain many frames; source drops and frame expiries cannot be summed as independent loss.
disposition: Rejected for production: zero receive admission pressure but unlimited CPU rises 27.7–30.0% left and 41.0–42.1% right for only 3.4–6.6% / 3.8–5.5% delivered-goodput gains. Unsent expiry increases roughly twofold. Fixed 21G load also shows substantially more CPU and expiry. No original performance gate passes.

checks: three kernel guard regressions and existing burst/admission tests
